newsitem.title: USA: Key IMM currencies down sharply after panicky open.
newsitem.headline: Key IMM currencies down sharply after panicky open.

text.p: Key IMM currency futures were sharply lower on brisk selling that turned panicky at the opening due to the dollar's overnight rally above critical resistance levels against the mark and yen, traders said.
"A lot of people are scared," one currency futures floor trader said after the opening of pit trade. "People just panicked and liquidated longs."

June yen set a contract low of $0.008032, immediately falling through the GLOBEX low of $0.008055 at the opening, while one firm sold 1,000 June marks within the first five minutes of trade, they said.
British press reports on Monday that Germany had relaxed its hard-line stance on the entry conditions for European monetary union (EMU) were the catalyst for the dollar's spike higher, traders said.
Two British newspapers carried stories that German Finance Minister Theo Waigel had softened his stance on a strict interpretation of the EMU budget criteria.
The newspaper articles gave many traders the impression that Germany would allow the mark to depreciate further.
One veteran currency trader said Waigel's subsequent denials did not diminish the market's impression.
Waigel denied the reports, and a ministry spokeswoman denied that Waigel had presented a changed view at a meeting of finance ministers this weekend at the Netherlands' resort of Noordwijk.
"I don't care that he denied those reports," the trader said. "It's not in Germany's best interest to fight a higher dollar/mark."
Several traders look for June marks to slip below the contract low of $0.5840 within days, and expect the contract to fall as low as $0.5743, or about 1.75 spot, within the next month.
One forex analyst with a large European bank said dollar/mark would remain in a range until it rallies through the 1.7250 spot area, which corresponds to $0.5826 in the June mark contract.
He said dollar/mark's ability to hold gains above 1.6850 spot last week was a positive technical development that added "fuel to the fire."

The wave of dollar enthusiasm emerged on Friday after U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said in Tokyo that Japan should not let its trade surplus surge. Rubin also said exchange rates should not be used as a trade tool.
On Sunday, Rubin said the strong dollar was helping the U.S. economy.
June yen fell through support at $0.008086 and $0.008054 on GLOBEX, and should test $0.007715 within the next month, near a dollar/yen rate of 131.00, traders said.

At 1015 CDT/1515 GMT, June yen was off $0.000100 at $0.008029, marks were off $0.0089 at $0.5877, Swiss francs were $0.0113 lower at $0.6872, sterling was down $0.0058 at $1.6272, Canadian dollars were up $0.0014 at $0.7228, and Australian dollars were up $0.0003 at $0.7753.
